subject.title: Control UI settings pages need one unified design language

question: Should the proposed flat section-and-row anatomy become the mandatory Control UI settings contract, and which page-specific exceptions and migration sequence should be supported?
rationale: Source inspection confirms the inconsistency, but choosing a mandatory visual contract and the boundary with the existing shared design-system project requires maintainer design intent.

options.title: Approve staged standardization
options.body: Adopt shared tokens and semantic settings primitives, document explicit exceptions, and migrate a few related pages per focused PR.

options.title: Consolidate primitives only
options.body: Unify controls, spacing tokens, and duplicate CSS while allowing settings pages to retain distinct layouts.

options.title: Retain page-owned design
options.body: Address concrete usability defects individually without establishing a mandatory settings anatomy.

recommendation.title: Approve staged standardization
recommendation.body: Adopt shared tokens and semantic settings primitives, document explicit exceptions, and migrate a few related pages per focused PR.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available routing signal is the prior merged design-system guidance and connection to the earlier Control UI audit.
